data.title: Tesla And SpaceX ‘Better Together’? Musk Leans Yes — But Says Performance Must Drive His TSLA Pay
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tesla’s 2025 pay package covers 423.7 million shares.
  • Musk said AI, robotics and chip design changed his view of a merger. The companies already work together on Terafab, which aims to produce its first test chip in May or June 2027.
  • An announcement could reportedly come as early as December or slip into early 2027.

Elon Musk said on Wednesday that Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) would probably be better together, but that closing a merger shouldn’t be enough to earn him the stock awards Tesla tied to its performance.

Both stocks rose for a second straight session on Wednesday, with TSLA gaining 1 % and SPCX climbing 1.3%.

Could A SpaceX Merger Unlock Musk’s Tesla Pay?

“You don’t need them to be together, but would they be better together?” Musk said at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit. “Probably yes.” Musk said advances in AI, robotics and chip design had given Tesla and SpaceX a reason to consider a combination that he struggled to see five years ago.

Andrew Ross Sorkin, a columnist for The New York Times, raised a question DealBook readers had repeatedly asked about whether a merger should trigger Musk’s Tesla stock awards. “I should not receive those stock option awards simply for merging with SpaceX because that is not meeting the deal, which was that I should only get those stock options for Tesla performance, not just because of a merger,” Musk said.

A merger could change how Musk earns his Tesla pay. He called the awards stock options, though Tesla’s filings say his 2025 package consists of 423.7 million shares of performance-based restricted stock. To earn each of the 12 installments, Tesla typically must hit an operating goal and a valuation target, starting at $2 trillion and rising to $8.5 trillion.

If the deal’s structure triggered Tesla’s change-in-control clause, shares Musk had already earned would vest. The deal price would factor into Tesla’s valuation, which alone would determine whether he earned more.

One way the clause could kick in is if a new owner gained more than half of Tesla’s voting power. An exception applies if Tesla’s existing shareholders keep at least half the voting power in Tesla or its parent company, with their stakes in about the same proportion as before.

To work out what Musk earned, Tesla would use whichever is higher: its last closing price or the price shareholders received in the deal. A higher deal could unlock more shares for Musk even if Tesla missed an operating goal. He would give up any part of the award he still had not earned when the deal closed.

How AI And Robotics Brought TSLA And SPCX Closer

“If you’d asked me five years ago, do I ever think there’s any purpose in SpaceX and Tesla getting together, I would have said no,” Musk said.

Tesla develops AI for self-driving cars and its Optimus robot, while SpaceX builds large AI models and supplies computing power to customers such as Anthropic. Both design advanced chips and already work together on Terafab, their chipmaking venture. Last month, Musk said Terafab was aiming to produce its first test chip in May or June 2027.

Who Gets The Final Say On TSLA-SPCX Merger?

However, Tesla and SpaceX could pursue the opportunities on their own, Musk said. The case for a merger hinges on whether they could create more value for shareholders together.

“These require shareholder votes, which may or may not succeed,” Musk said. He added that his own vote would have to take into account whether the terms made financial sense for other SpaceX investors.

Musk confirmed last month that both companies had formed committees of independent directors to explore a deal. An announcement could reportedly come as early as December, but the companies had also discussed early 2027.

Before Musk confirmed the merger talks in October, Goldman Sachs had expanded its Tesla options positions while cutting its stake in the automaker by 11.7%. By the end of September, its calls covered 5.66 million Tesla shares, up 186.5% from June. Its puts also nearly doubled to cover 5.24 million shares.

Retail Traders Split Over What Tesla Brings To A Deal

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘neutral’ on TSLA amid ‘low’ message volume and ‘bullish’ on SPCX amid ‘normal’ message volume.

One user said, “$TSLA the street is expecting details from MERGER meetings..so keep your eyes open MM playing games volume facts.. MERGER is HERE”

View this Stocktwits post

Another user said, “$TSLA The SpaceX merger committee will not approve a merger with a company that has a 415P. E! It would be illegal, it would be considered fraud. Either the merger will not happen, or they have to drop. Tesla down to a reasonable number, maybe below 200.”

View this Stocktwits post

So far this year, TSLA shares are down 15%, while SPCX shares are up 6% from their June IPO price.

data.title: Trump administration unveils new center to choke off scam payments
data.description:
The Trump administration has unveiled a new Threat Disruption Center, aimed at stopping money flows to foreign criminal networks behind scams, cybercrime and sextortion schemes.

The Homeland Security Task Force’s National Coordination Center, co-led by the departments of Homeland Security and Justice, announced the launch of the unit on Wednesday. It seeks to help more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners track scams and work with banks and crypto platforms to stop payments to scam networks.

The Homeland Security statement said the center was created under a March 2026 executive order that directed federal agencies to work with private companies to combat online fraud and other cybercrime targeting Americans.

“Every hour between a victim’s report and a response gives criminals more time to launder stolen funds and identify their next target,” said Heith Janke, operations director of the FBI’s Criminal Branch.

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs was selected as the center’s main private-sector partner. It will provide and maintain Ardence, the investigative platform the center will use to map scam networks and identify victims. TRM said it will also provide engineering and investigative support.

“These scammers rarely stop after one payment — they drain a victim’s savings, or their retirement, over months and years,” said Esteban Castano, co-founder and CEO of TRM Labs.

“Stepping in sooner changes everything: a warning before the next payment, a scam website removed before it victimizes another family, or stolen funds frozen while they can still be recovered.

The FBI received about 453,000 reports of online fraud in 2025, with reported losses exceeding $17.7 billion.

In September, the Justice Department estimated that overseas scam centers cost Americans about $10 billion a year through schemes including crypto and online investment fraud.

data.title: Japan equities fall as investors await Anthropic listing
data.description:
By Satoshi Sugiyama

Japanese equities fell on Thursday as investors awaited Anthropic’s highly anticipated US listing, while falling metal prices weighed on nonferrous metal stocks.

The Nikkei 225 Index reversed earlier gains and fell 0.3% to 58,850.70, as of 0138 GMT. The broader Topix slid 0.64% to 3,799.41.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its targeted range of $70 to $78 per share, in one of the largest stock market IPOs on record and the first by a major frontier AI model developer.

Reuters separately reported Anthropic’s IPO raised $81.31 billion on Wednesday, eclipsing SpaceX’s offering to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record. The shares will begin trading on the ​Nasdaq on Thursday.

"Anthropic’s IPO is pending, and a US-China-Russia summit is scheduled (later in the day) ... so market participants are likely to hold back from aggressive trading while they wait to see how events unfold,” analysts at Tokai Tokyo Intelligence Laboratory said in a note.

US shares were mixed overnight with Nvidia falling nearly 3% despite quarterly results that beat analyst expectations, as investors weighed uncertainty over co-founder Jensen Huang’s exit.

In Tokyo, AI- and chip-related shares mostly fell, with Advantest losing 1.88% and Fujikura falling 3.9%.

Japan’s nonferrous metal index slid to its lowest level in a year as gold prices fell to a 14-month low and copper dropped to its weakest in seven months.

JX Advanced Metals , Mitsubishi Materials and Mitsui Kinzoku were the biggest percentage decliners on the Nikkei, down 7.11%, 6.08% and 5.80%, respectively.

On the other hand, Trend Micro was the biggest percentage gainer on the Nikkei, rising 4.99%, followed by J. Front Retailing , up 3.86%, and Daikin Industries , up 3.49%.

data.title: Barbados readies landmark 'debt-for-health' swap
data.description:
Key points:
  • Barbados to buy back $600 million of 2018 restructuring bonds
  • New 20-year loans carry 3.25% average interest rate versus 7% to 8%
  • Swap to channel $160 million of debt savings into health system

By Marc Jones

Barbados laid out plans for a landmark new "debt-for-health" swap on Wednesday, which will funnel $160 million worth of high-interest debt savings into the Caribbean country's strained health system.

The deal marks the first time such a swap has been done with commercial market debt and the first to use a new standardised "debt-for-resilience" facility launched last year to help small, low-income economies fund priority projects they may otherwise struggle to afford.

The set-up is backed by the Inter-American Development Bank, the World Bank, CAF and the Caribbean Development Bank.

Under the plan, Barbados will buy back $600 million ⁠of the bonds it sold when it restructured its debt in 2018. ​It will then refinance them with new 20-year bank loans with a far lower ​average interest rate of just 3.25%, compared to 7%-8%.

That is possible thanks to the four development banks' "credit guarantees" that effectively reduce the risk for those providing the new loans.

"This is significant because of how impactful we expect it to be," Barbados' health and wellness minister, Lisa Cummins, told reporters on a conference call.

Debt swaps have become increasingly popular in recent years as a way for developing countries to replace expensive debt and use the savings on projects such as environmental conservation, schools or infrastructure.

But the new debt-for-resilience mechanism is a leap forward as it largely standardises many of the legal and transactional complexities that have meant some recent swaps have taken years to execute and produced relatively modest debt savings.

Barbados' Finance Minister Ryan Straughn highlighted that this one, which will help fund a partial rebuild of its main hospital in Bridgetown as well as improve other health services, has taken less than a year to put together.

As well as being the first "debt-for-health" swap involving market debt, the $600 million size of the debt swap is estimated to be the highest on record, equating to around 7% of Barbados' GDP.

It is also the first time four development banks have joined forces on a single debt swap.

Avinash Persaud, special adviser at the Inter-American Development Bank, said all the development banks had worked "surprisingly well" together and that they stood ready to do more.

Straughn added that he was already looking at Barbados' next one and that everyone involved wanted them to be a blueprint for other small, indebted countries to replicate.

"Any country in any hemisphere can use this framework," Straughn said.

data.title: U.S. Offers $50 Million to Support Malaysia's Sovereign AI Cloud Initiative
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

KUALA LUMPUR--The U.S. plans to help develop Malaysia's sovereign artificial-intelligence cloud, including through the participation of U.S. technology firms.

President Donald Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced the cooperation on Wednesday.

Trump is in Shenzhen this week as part of his visit to China for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings.

The U.S. indicated its intention to provided $50 million in financing for Malaysia's initiative, as well as technical assistance and training, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said.

The move comes as Malaysia seeks to establish itself as a regional AI hub, attracting billions of dollars in investment from global technology companies amid growing demand for computing power and cloud services.

In budget 2026, the government allocated 2 billion ringgit, or about $486 million, to establish the sovereign AI cloud, underscoring its push to build domestic AI infrastructure and ensure greater control over data and computing resources.

Write to Ying Xian Wong at yingxian.wong@wsj.com

data.title: Eden Innovations Sees Sustained EdenCrete Demand from US Customers
data.description:
Eden Innovations has reported continued US demand for its EdenCrete carbon nanotube-enriched liquid concrete additives, booking $795,000 in new orders through subsidiary Eden US during the first seven weeks of the quarter.

$302,000 of the orders came from ready-mix concrete (RMC) plants in Colorado, exceeding $121,000 in total EdenCrete sales recorded for the entire September quarter.

A $475,000 order for EdenCrete Pz7 from South American concrete producer Holcim Ecuador SA takes that customer’s cumulative orders since May 2024 to more than $1.47 million.

Eden executive chair Gregory H Solomon said new orders received during the reporting period demonstrated “strong and growing demand” for EdenCrete products.

RMC Plant Installations

There are currently 34 RMC plants across the US, Ecuador, and Canada that have EdenCrete bulk storage and dispensing installations, with the four most recent contracts being in Colorado and Texas.

Each installation allows a plant to accurately dispense low dosages of EdenCrete additives into its concrete mixes, and it can often take several months for dosages and mix designs to be optimised before an additive is fully integrated into daily operations.

Plant owners typically become regular users of EdenCrete products and place replenishment orders as their use increases.

The current level of activity in Colorado—where many RMC plants have been early adopters of EdenCrete—is seen by the company as a leading indicator of how the broader North American installation base is expected to develop over coming quarters.

Eden’s presence in Ecuador provides the company with a strong foothold, a reference customer and practical operating experience in South America.

Enhanced Concrete Performance

Eden’s range of EdenCrete products (standard, Pz, and Pz7) are designed to enhance concrete performance characteristics including abrasion resistance, reduced permeability, increased modulus of elasticity, reduced shrinkage, and compressive, flexural, and tensile strength.

These benefits can deliver more durable concrete with a longer service life and a lower life-cycle carbon footprint.

EdenCrete Pz and Pz7 are most frequently used in concrete mixes that incorporate a higher percentage of pozzolans as an alternative cementitious material, such as fly-ash and blast furnace slag—waste by-products of coal-fired power stations and metal smelting respectively.

This enables a material proportion of total Portland cement in concrete mixes to be replaced by the same percentage of pozzolans without any loss in performance.

Since 2015, EdenCrete has been used in US applications including medium and high-rise building construction, as well as new roads and bridges.

data.title: Japan futures fall for third session as oil slips, tyre output slides
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Japanese rubber futures fell for a third straight session on Thursday, tracking lower oil prices, while lacklustre tyre output also weighed on the market.

  • The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for April delivery , was down 2.5 yen, or 0.58%, at 428.1 yen ($2.69) per kg as of 0127 GMT

  • The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery fell 360 yuan, or 1.88%, to 18,800 yuan ($2,819.61) per metric ton

  • The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) lost 270 yuan, or 1.74%, to 15,265 yuan per metric ton

  • Top consumer China's rubber tyre output fell 4.6% year-on-year to 94.15 million units in October, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed

  • Oil prices settled down more than 1% on Wednesday after US crude and fuel inventories posted larger-than-expected rises, according to the Energy Information Administration, adding to expectations of a supply surplus

data.title: Stocks rise after Anthropic IPO pricing sets stage for blockbuster debut
data.description:
By Ankur Banerjee

Asian equities and US stock futures rose on Thursday after Claude chatbot maker Anthropic scored the biggest IPO ever with an $81 billion offering ahead of its market debut in a test for the AI trade that has been under pressure in recent weeks.

Japan's Nikkei rose 1% in early trading while Nasdaq futures gained 1% and S&P futures were 0.6% higher after Anthropic said the IPO was priced at $83 apiece, above its previously targeted range.

On a fully diluted basis, the IPO values Anthropic, the first major frontier AI model developer to go public, at about $1.5 trillion and its first-day trading will be scrutinised to gauge investor sentiment on the technology.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said it was going to be a huge test for the markets and it looked poised to be a really bullish listing.

"I don't think it's necessarily going to assuage all the fears about AI. I think much of that boils down to future investment growth ... However, if the stock trades the way it looks like it will, it might calm the market a bit."

Investor confidence in AI has been shaken in the past few weeks on worries about the profitability of the technology and the massive debt needed to fund and build AI infrastructure.

Markets mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia this week as uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors. The company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang.

The market mood remained fragile with South Korea's Kospi flat while Taiwan stocks TWSE:TAIEX were 1% lower. That left MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) down 0.3%, set for a decline of over 4% for the week.

In currencies, the dollar was on the front foot as hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller bolstered expectations of an interest rate hike in December.

The euro was at $1.0978, hovering near its lowest since April 2025. The Japanese yen was at 157.42 per US dollar and sterling fetched $1.31515.

Waller said on CNBC that if the central bank wanted to get inflation down it needed to take more "aggressive action" either through a half-point increase at the December meeting, or by using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes.

The comments come after hotter-than-expected inflation data last week, leaving markets bracing for a rate hike. Traders are pricing in a 90% chance of a 25 basis points hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

"More hawkish Fed pricing has so far offset weakness in technology stocks, keeping the USD supported," OCBC strategists said in a note. "Persistent inflation, further Fed tightening and elevated US yields suggest it is still too early to bet against the USD."

In commodities, oil prices remained under pressure as the growing view that the oil market is turning to a surplus weighed. Brent crude futures were 0.58% lower at $91.47 a barrel, set for a third straight weekly decline.

data.title: Australia's Jobless Rate Rises to Highest Level Since 2021 — Update
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--Australia's unemployment rate jumped in October to its highest level since late 2021, highlighting fears that the economy is slowing rapidly due to weak confidence and five interest-rate increases since the start of the year.

Unemployment hit 4.9% in October, up from 4.7% in September, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Thursday.

The economy lost 43,500 jobs in October, with part-time employment falling by 40,600.

Higher unemployment will argue strongly for the Reserve Bank of Australia to keep interest rates on hold from here, albeit data on Wednesday showed wages grew at their fastest pace since 2023 in the third quarter.

RBA Gov. Michele Bullock also affirmed this week her view that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Inflation data for October will be released next week, with economists warning that there is a high risk that it will once again surprise on the high side of estimates.

Still, the impact of interest-rate increases this year is becoming increasingly obvious, with lending for new homes collapsing and house prices heading toward record losses.

The RBA has talked about the difficult policy task before, highlighting that elevated inflation remains its main priority.

The bank recently forecast that inflation will remain above target until mid-2028, amid concerns inflation expectations are becoming embedded.

"With the labor market continuing to weaken rapidly, we remain comfortable in our view that the RBA won't tighten policy any further," said Abhijit Surya, senior economist at Capital Economics.

The employment-to-population ratio fell 0.3 percentage point to 63.3%, and the participation rate fell 0.2 percentage point to 66.6%

The number of hours worked fell 0.2% in October, while the underemployment rate fell 0.1 percentage point to 6.2%.

The Australian dollar fell on the data to 66.90 U.S. cents from around 67.20 U.S. cents.

Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com

data.title: Australia shares recoup losses after weak jobs data backs RBA hold
data.description:
Australian shares recouped some early losses on Thursday after weak labour market data bolstered expectations of a pause by the central bank in December, as employment fell sharply and the jobless rate rose to a five-year high.

The S&P/ASX 200 index was down 0.7% at 8,762.00 points, as of 0044 GMT, after falling as much as 1.3% earlier in the session.

Domestic employment fell for a second consecutive month in October, with Australian Bureau of Statistics data showing net employment declined by 43,500 after a drop of 36,400 in September.

The weaker-than-expected jobs data pointed to easing labour market tightness, offering some relief to investors concerned over potential rate hikes by the Reserve Bank of Australia.

Swaps now imply a 98% chance of the existing policy being held as it is next month, while the chances of a rate cut went up to 2% from zero.

Banks were trading 0.4% lower, extending losses to a third consecutive session.

Among the "Big Four" lenders, National Australia Bank fell the most with a 0.8% drop.

Miners declined 3.2% to their weakest level since late March as copper prices slumped to a seven-month low.

The sub-index has shed roughly 14% over the past few sessions despite a mild recovery in iron ore futures in the previous session.

Shares of BHP fell 2.8% to an early-April low on Thursday, while Rio Tinto declined 1.8%

Gold stocks shed 4.9% as hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve pushed gold to a 14-month low, reinforcing expectations that interest rates will remain higher for longer.

Shares of Northern Star Resources and Evolution Mining were down 3% each.

Technology stocks rose 0.8%, tracking overnight gains on the tech-heavy Nasdaq after chipmaker Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above estimates.

Shares of Xero fell 0.5%.

Farther south-east, New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index fell 0.2% to 14,264.29 points.

data.title: JLL Receives Frost & Sullivan's 2026 North American Competitive Strategy Leadership Recognition for Facility Management
data.description:
JLL is recognized for transforming facility management through an integrated Workplace Management platform, digital innovation, and sector-focused execution that strengthens operational resilience and business performance.

SAN ANTONIO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As facility management continues to evolve from a largely operational function into a strategic contributor to workplace performance and enterprise resilience, JLL is demonstrating how an integrated approach can create measurable value for organizations across complex environments. Frost & Sullivan recognizes JLL with the 2026 North American Competitive Strategy Leadership Recognition in Facility Management for its ability to combine strategic transformation, digital capabilities, and sector expertise to strengthen its competitive position and deliver integrated facility management (IFM) solutions across the region.

Frost & Sullivan evaluates companies through a rigorous benchmarking process across two core dimensions: strategy effectiveness and strategy execution. JLL excelled in both, demonstrating its ability to align strategic initiatives with evolving market demands while executing them with consistency, scale, and measurable impact. "JLL is a recognized leader in IFM and workplace solutions across North America. Its competitive position is built on a clear strategic progression: redefining Facility Management through the Workplace Management platform, aligning its operating structure to support integrated delivery, and scaling digital and sector-specific capabilities across the United States and Canada. This approach enables JLL to serve commercial office, financial services, life sciences, technology, industrial and advanced manufacturing, data centers, healthcare, and government clients while linking facility operations more directly to business performance," said Janice Wung, Industry Principal, Homes & Buildings, Frost & Sullivan.

JLL's strategic approach centers on its Workplace Management platform, which brings together facilities management, technical services, sustainable operations, safety, sourcing and procurement, workplace experience, and technology-enabled delivery under a single operating structure. The platform supports greater standardization, governance, and scalability across multi-site portfolios while maintaining flexibility for sector-specific requirements.

Digital innovation further differentiates JLL's approach to facility management. Technologies, including Corrigo, JLL Smart Building Platform, Azara, and JLL Falcon AI, support work order and asset management, predictive maintenance, energy optimization, workplace analytics, and portfolio-level performance visibility. These capabilities enable clients to move beyond reactive facility operations toward more proactive, data-driven decision-making.

"We are honored Frost & Sullivan is recognizing JLL's work in facilities management," said Chris Fernandez, Americas Head of Workplace Management at JLL. "At its core, facilities management is about creating environments where people can do their best work while ensuring the buildings they depend on operate safely, reliably and efficiently every day. FM has evolved far beyond maintaining physical assets. Today, it sits at the intersection of workplace experience, operational resilience and business performance. data.title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO opens today: Should you subscribe to the ₹8,981 crore issue?
data.description:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. (MCL), a wholly owned subsidiary of state-run Coal India Ltd., will open for subscription on November 19 and close on November 23.

Mahanadi Coalfields has raised ₹2,295.2 crore through its anchor book, ahead of the IPO opening for public subscription on Thursday, November 19.

Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) emerged as the largest investor, accounting for more than 26% of the total anchor allocation. Nippon Life India was another major participant, investing nearly ₹500 crore.

The company allotted 16.87 crore equity shares to 53 institutional investors at ₹136 per share, the upper end of the IPO price band, on November 18.

Of the total allocation, 8.95 crore shares were allotted to 11 domestic mutual funds, including Nippon Life India, WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund, Invesco India, Tata Mutual Fund, HDFC AMC, ICICI Prudential AMC, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC and Axis Mutual Fund, according to a regulatory filing.

Five insurance companies collectively invested ₹605.24 crore to acquire 4.45 crore shares. LIC accounted for the bulk of this investment, purchasing 4.17 crore shares worth approximately ₹568 crore.

Other prominent institutional investors participating in the anchor book included Ashoka WhiteOak ICAV, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Societe Generale, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and Integrated Core Strategies (Asia).

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: What brokerages recommend

PL Capital: The brokerage said Mahanadi Coalfields offers a trailing dividend yield of 8.5% at the IPO price, compared with 6.6% for Coal India in FY26, making the issue attractive from a cash-return perspective.

At the proposed IPO market capitalisation of around ₹90,000 crore, Mahanadi Coalfields is valued at a 10-15% premium to Coal India's FY26 valuation multiple of 5 times. PL Capital said the premium appears justified by MCL's relatively stronger operating profitability and return ratios, as well as its focused capital allocation.

The brokerage pointed to an EBITDA CAGR of 6% for MCL between FY20 and FY26, compared with 5% for Coal India. It has recommended subscribing to the issue from a medium- to long-term perspective.

Anand Rathi: The brokerage has assigned a ‘Subscribe – Long Term’ rating to the IPO, citing Mahanadi Coalfields' market leadership, extensive reserve life, low-cost mechanised operations, strong profitability and infrastructure-led growth plans.

However, it also flagged the structural and regulatory risks associated with coal mining.

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO details

Mahanadi Coalfields has fixed the IPO price band at ₹129-₹136 per equity share. Investors can bid for a minimum of 110 shares and in multiples thereof.

At the upper end of the price band, the company is targeting a valuation of ₹90,009.74 crore. The IPO is expected to raise ₹8,981.12 crore.

The issue is entirely an offer for sale (OFS), through which Coal India plans to divest 66.18 crore shares, representing a 10% stake in Mahanadi Coalfields.

Since the IPO does not involve a fresh issue of shares, Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any proceeds from the offering. The entire amount raised, after applicable expenses, will go to Coal India.

Of the total issue, 50% has been reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 15% for non-institutional investors (NIIs) and the remaining 35% for retail investors.

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO GMP

Mahanadi Coalfields' IPO was commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of ₹3.1 per share on Thursday morning. This represents a premium of around 2.28% over the upper end of the IPO price band of ₹136.

At the prevailing GMP, the estimated listing price works out to ₹139.1 per share.

However, grey market premiums are indicative of investor sentiment in the unofficial market and can fluctuate significantly before listing. They do not guarantee the listing price or actual market performance.

Mahanadi Coalfields: Biz and financial performance

Mahanadi Coalfields primarily operates in Odisha and accounted for 21% of India's total domestic coal production and 28.4% of Coal India's output in FY26.

Coal India, meanwhile, contributed around 74% of India's total coal production during the financial year.

In March, the state-run mining company had indicated plans to divest stakes of up to 25% in Mahanadi Coalfields and South Eastern Coalfields through IPOs or other routes.

For the financial year ended March 31, Mahanadi Coalfields reported a 1.3% year-on-year decline in net profit to ₹10,678 crore. Its revenue fell 2.6% to ₹30,550 crore.

Coal India has already listed two of its subsidiaries on the stock exchanges this year. Bharat Coking Coal, which made its market debut in January, is trading around 25% below its listing price. Central Mine Planning & Design Institute, which listed in March, has gained approximately 39% since its debut.

DIPAM Secy on Mahanadi Coalfields IPO valuation, dividends

Coal India and its soon-to-be-listed subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields are expected to remain consistent dividend-paying companies, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Arunish Chawla told CNBC-TV18 in an exclusive interaction on November 16.

His comments came shortly after Mahanadi Coalfields announced the price band for its ₹8,981 crore IPO.

Describing the valuation as "fair" and "restrained", Chawla said the government wanted to ensure that investors had an opportunity to benefit from the offering.

"The idea is to leave something on the table for the investors. It has been done with that perspective, and the investors should also remember that Coal India and its subsidiaries and Mahanadi Coalfields are high dividend-paying stocks, and they pay regular dividends to their shareholders," the DIPAM Secretary said.

He added that investors should consider the companies' dividend-paying track records while evaluating their growth prospects.

Mahanadi Coalfields has distributed more than ₹25,750 crore in dividends over FY24, FY25 and FY26. It paid ₹8,600 crore in FY24, ₹8,750 crore in FY25 and ₹8,400 crore in FY26.

Under the government's guidelines, each profitable public sector undertaking (PSU) is required to pay a minimum annual dividend of 30% of its profit after tax (PAT) or 4% of its net worth, whichever is higher.

However, the company's ability to maintain these payouts will depend on its financial performance and capital requirements.

In its red herring prospectus (RHP), Mahanadi Coalfields said: "The Company's ability to declare and pay dividends going forward will depend upon its future financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, profit after tax available for distribution, working capital requirements, capital expenditure plans, and the restrictive covenants of its financing arrangements."

SBI Capital Markets, Axis Capital, BOB Capital Markets, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities and IIFL Capital Services are the merchant bankers managing the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO.

The equity shares of Mahanadi Coalfields are proposed to be listed on both the BSE and the NSE.

data.title: India's power demand surges as coal stocks run critically low
data.description:
India's electricity demand rose 11.7% year-on-year in the first seven months of FY2027, while coal stocks at thermal power stations sat well under half the required level, according to rating agency ICRA , ET EnergyWorld reported on November 18.

Thermal plants held roughly seven days of coal as of November 11, against a norm of 19 to 20 days. That leaves generators little room to absorb an abrupt jump in consumption or any interruption to fuel deliveries, ICRA said in its assessment.

The thin stockpiles persist even though coal shipments to the power sector grew 5.1% year-on-year in the first half of FY2027. Domestic output slipped 1.1% over those six months, with weaker production at state-run Coal India Limited the main drag.

ICRA warned that if inventories shrink further, especially alongside softer domestic output or supply bottlenecks, power producers could struggle to cope with a steep rise in peak demand. The agency said a lasting recovery in coal production and deliveries would be needed to rebuild adequate stocks.

November has brought no letup in rising consumption: according to Grid Controller of India Limited data, demand during the month's opening 11 days was 12.9% higher than in the same period a year earlier.

Warmer than usual weather across much of the country has kept cooling loads high even as winter sets in. Festival-season activity, steady industrial and commercial use and strong farm demand have also pushed consumption up.

ICRA forecasts electricity demand growth of about 8.5% for the full FY2027, though it named weather as a major risk to that projection.

Spot prices have eased from October as supply improved, notably during solar generation hours. The average tariff on the Indian Energy Exchange was INR4 ($0.043) per unit as of November 10, compared with INR6.7 in October 2026. That was still above the INR3.1 per unit recorded in November 2025, with healthy demand keeping prices supported.

ICRA said tariffs for the rest of FY2027 would hinge on how the balance between supply and demand develops and how quickly new generating capacity comes online.
